deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of Riemann's aether theory of gravitation and light. Riemann published nothing on it himself; a cleaner version appears as the fragment 'Gravitation und Licht' in the Nachlass section of his Werke (1876, ed. Dedekind/Weber). Notation: η = (η1,η2,η3) are coordinates of geometric space. η' = (η1',η2',η3') is a vector field describing the motion of the 'physical space' (the aether). Σ1 denotes summation over the three components. cc = c².

(1) Top lines. On preceding (unseen) pages Riemann evidently set X_i = c²Δη_i' − ∂²η_i'/∂t², with X_i the 'force' components. Here he states X_i = ∂λ/∂η_i (i = 1,2,3), so X = ∇λ. He then identifies λ = ∂²V/∂t² ('Bedeutung des λ', the meaning of λ). This presupposes the earlier ansatz η' = ∇V together with the incompressibility condition div η' = ΔV = 0 in empty space. [My reconstruction:] then c²Δ∇V − ∇V_tt = ∇(c²ΔV − V_tt) = −∇V_tt. So λ = ±V_tt up to an additive function of t; the sign depends on the sign convention for X, which is not visible on this page.

(2) Variational reformulation ('ein noch allgemeinerer Ausdruck'). Let δη' be a variation with div δη' = 0 that vanishes on the boundary. Then Σ∫X_i δη_i' dη dt = ∫∇λ·δη' = −∫λ div δη' = 0. This step is implicit. Writing X out gives Σ∫{c²Δη_i' − ∂²η_i'/∂t²} δη_i' dη dt = 0. Integration by parts in space and time ('···' standing for the boundary terms) turns this into −Σ∫{c²∇η_i'·∇δη_i' − ∂_tη_i' ∂_tδη_i'} dη dt. That equals −½ δ Σ∫{c²|∇η_i'|² − (∂_tη_i')²} dη dt; Riemann drops the ½, which is harmless since the expression = 0.

Riemann's verbal reading of this: the points of physical space move so that this space, regarded as a substance, never changes its density (div η' = 0). In addition, the 'sum of squares of the changes of the motion' becomes a minimum. In modern terms, the action ∫(|η'_t|² − c²|∇η'|²) is stationary under divergence-free variations. The incompressibility constraint is handled with the multiplier λ, which plays the role of a pressure.

(3) General law for all of geometric space, empty or filled with ponderable matter:
0 = δ[ Σ∫{(∂_tη_i')² − c²|∇η_i'|²} dη dt − ∫λ div η' dη dt − ∫λ dm dt + ∫dm Σ(ẋ_i or ẍ_i)² dt ].
Here dm is the ponderable mass element located at (x1,x2,x3) at time t, with arbitrary units. λ is an arbitrary function of place: the first λ is expressed in the η's, the second in the x's.

- Varying λ gives div η' dη + dm = 0, i.e. div η' ∝ −ρ. The next page states this as div η' = −4πρ: matter acts as a source or sink of the aether.
- Varying η' gives the forced wave equation η'_tt − c²Δη' = −∇λ, up to sign.
- Varying x gives the equation of motion of matter in the potential λ. On the next page Riemann uses squared accelerations, which leads to fourth time derivatives.

(4) In matter-free space, where matter has no motion, only the first two terms remain: an incompressible, wave-carrying medium. The next page interprets this as giving the laws of light, and as giving the cause of gravitation via the source condition.
errors: The factor 1/2 is omitted when passing from Σ∫(c²∇η'·∇δη' − η'_t δη'_t) to δΣ∫(c²|∇η'|² − η'_t²); this is immaterial because the expression is set to zero.
'Minimum' is not justified: the functional ∫(η'_t² − c²|∇η'|²) is indefinite, so the condition is only stationarity (an extremum or saddle), not a minimum.
The step Σ∫X_i δη_i' = 0 silently requires the variations δη' to be divergence-free and to vanish at the boundary (integration by parts against ∇λ); Riemann does not state this.
λ = ∂²V/∂t² holds only up to sign/convention and an additive function of t, and only if η' = ∇V with ΔV = 0 (or ΔV absorbed into λ). This presupposition is not visible on this page.

In the general equation the multiplier term ∫λ dm dt and the matter term are dimensionally and sign-wise loosely matched; the coupling constant (4π) appears only on the next page. Whether the matter term is a velocity or an acceleration squared is inconsistent with the next page, where accelerations squared lead to an unusual 4th-order equation ∂λ/∂y = ∂⁴y/∂t⁴.

results.what: Equation of motion of the aether as a wave equation with gradient forcing: c²Δη' − η'_tt = ∇λ, with div η' = 0
results.modern_name: Incompressible elastic-aether wave equation with a pressure Lagrange multiplier (transverse waves)
results.usually_credited_to: Elastic-solid aether theories of Cauchy, Green (1838), MacCullagh (1839), Stokes

results.what: Variational (Hamilton-principle) formulation δ∫(η'_t² − c²|∇η'|²) − ∫λ div η' = 0, with λ a Lagrange multiplier enforcing constant density
results.modern_name: Hamilton's principle with a Lagrange multiplier for an incompressibility constraint

results.what: Unified Lagrangian coupling aether and ponderable matter, with matter as a source of aether divergence (div η' = −4πρ on the next page), to explain gravitation and light together
results.modern_name: Aether (sink/source) model of gravitation; precursor of field-theoretic action principles for matter + field
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann's fragment 'Gravitation und Licht' (Werke 1876); related sink theories later by Bjerknes and Pearson

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material already published in the Nachlass of Riemann's Werke ('Gravitation und Licht'), where the same incompressible aether, the multiplier λ and the source condition div η' = −4πρ appear. The page adds draft-level variants (the explicit variational form including the matter term) but nothing beyond what historians already attribute to him.

checkable.asserts: If η' = ∇V then c²Δη' − η'_tt = ∇(c²ΔV − V_tt), so X is a gradient (gives 0).

checkable.asserts: The first variation of (u_t² − c²u_x²) is 2(u_t δu_t − c² u_x δu_x), showing the omitted factor 2 (gives 0).

transcription_corrections: The final matter term ∫dm((∂x1/∂t)² + ...) dt may read (∂²x1/∂t²)² in the manuscript (the image shows second-derivative-like denominators ∂t²); the next page uses accelerations squared, so the transcription's first derivatives are doubtful.
The interlinear insertion above 'Bewegungsart' is probably 'jedesmaligen' or similar; the phrase reads 'die Summen der Quadrate der Änderungen der ... Bewegungsart'.
'(Bedeutung des λ)' is written to the right of λ = ∂²V/∂t²; the transcription is correct.

In the general equation the λ-divergence term is the full div η' = ∂η1'/∂η1 + ∂η2'/∂η2 + ∂η3'/∂η3 (not repeated η1'), as in the transcription; the deleted words '[-für den ganzen-] [-die überall eine-]' precede 'geometrischen Raum'.
Line 'zur Zeit t sich befindende ponderable Massenelement, dessen Einheit noch beliebig' is followed by an insertion 'und' replacing a struck word; the transcription is consistent with this.
